To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EEG microstates A, B, and C are decreased during TM practice compared to undirected thinking, while microstate D is increased during TM practice compared with undirected thinking, and that these effects are more pronounced during the phase of transcending than during the phase of undirected thinking.

the microstate classes A and C were more prominent in the EEG during the practice of TM, while the microstate class D was less prominent, than during undirected mentation and that these microstate classes are associated with different functional states of consciousness.
during TM practice the EEG microstates of classes A, B and C are decreased in duration and coverage and that the EEG microstates from class D are increased in duration and coverage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the functional significance of EEG microstates in the context of TM.
the identification and quantification of microstates of EEG activity during meditation and the comparison of these microstates with those observed during resting and task-free mental activity.
the question of what happens to the EEG during the practice of Transcendence Meditation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microstate classes A, B, and D are related to a more detached processing, whereas the microstate class C is related to a more salient, evaluative and self-referential processing.
the EEG microstate analysis of TM practice shows increased reference to reality, decreased saliency and increased detachment from internally generated mentations.
the TM technique is characterized by a specific pattern of brain activity which is different from the pattern during resting, undirected mentation, and during task performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EEG microstate analysis is a promising methodological approach for the investigation of the effects of meditation practices on the brain.
the TM practice appears to be characterized by an increase in the reference to reality and a decrease in internally generated mentations.
EEG microstate analysis is a useful tool for investigating the neurophysiological effects of meditation and other contemplative practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EEG microstates are altered during TM and these alterations may be related to the effects of TM on brain and behavior.
EEG microstate analysis is a promising approach to investigate the neural mechanisms of different meditation techniques.
TM is a unique form of meditation that is associated with specific EEG microstate changes.
